resources.string: Nothing to type: the car hotspot settings are imported; when the car has none, DiPlay writes its own details there after your confirmation, and devices using this hotspot may have to reconnect. Needs ADB on Android 11 and newer; not available on Android 8 to 10.
Importing the car hotspot details is not supported on this Android version.
The car hotspot now uses the DiPlay password.

The car\'s saved hotspot configuration could not be read. Continuing overwrites it with the DiPlay hotspot details: the hotspot name may change, the password is replaced, and other connected devices have to re-enter the password.
Nothing could be read from the car and DiPlay has no hotspot details yet. Continuing creates a new hotspot name and password in the car; other devices have to enter the new password.
DiPlay\'s hotspot password is written to the car\'s hotspot settings. Devices using this hotspot may have to re-enter the password.
Applied the next time the car hotspot starts
DiPlay could not write the car hotspot settings. The name and password stay unchanged.
A WPA3 hotspot is kept unchanged. Save the hotspot details with WPA2 to write them to the car.
An open hotspot in DiPlay does not overwrite the car\'s password.
Keys from a paired Bluetooth keyboard, remote or rotary controller move and select in CarPlay, like a car’s rotary knob. The touchscreen keeps working. Applies at once.

How much charging current DiPlay offers the iPhone over USB. If wired CarPlay drops every few seconds and the iPhone reconnects by itself, the car\'s USB port may not supply enough power: try Reduced, then Low. The iPhone then charges more slowly. Applies at the next USB connection.

Detected %1$s for the selected video format. Uses a dedicated MTK low-latency decoder when available. Legacy OMX decoders instead try no-reorder plus low latency, then low latency alone. Automatically falls back if the decoder rejects or fails. It may reduce video delay, but some firmware can stutter or fail. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.
Control is off. The car keeps its own lamp colors, brightness and area.
Music playing · %1$s: the lamps follow the music, up to level %2$d.
Music playing · %1$s: the lamps stay on one fixed color at level %2$d.
Paused, stopped or disconnected: every zone drops to the lowest level, which can switch the lamps off.
Paused, stopped or disconnected · %1$s: the lamps stay on the chosen color at level %2$d.
No music for 15 seconds: the lamps go back to the car’s own settings, and DiPlay takes over again when music starts.
The other zone is not changed while music plays.
Level 0: every zone stays at the lowest level, which can switch the lamps off.
Turn control off to hand the lamps back to the car’s own settings.
Colors change with how loud the music is.
Colors change at the estimated tempo (BPM).
Colors change on bass hits and strong beats.
Tap the colors the lamps may use. They change between your selection.
Tap the color to use. Fixed mode shows one color.
Colors come from the album cover. Turn off Follow album cover to pick colors yourself.

While CarPlay music plays, the car\'s own ambient-light music rhythm runs, with the colours and effects set in the car\'s ambient-light menu, where its music rhythm must be on. DiPlay does not set the lamps itself meanwhile. Checked when switched on. Needs the car\'s network ADB only where the head unit does not let DiPlay start the rhythm itself.
The car\'s music rhythm is not available: DiPlay cannot start it itself, and DiPlay\'s network ADB access or the head unit\'s audio service call is missing. Nothing was saved.
Send music data to the car\'s rhythm (older head units)

On some head units (such as a 2023 Han) the car\'s rhythm starts but stays dark, because the car makes no spectrum of its own for CarPlay music. This sends the played music\'s 16 frequency bands to the car\'s lamp controller, so the car\'s own rhythm, including the passenger dash, follows it. Only has an effect when the car\'s own music rhythm above is on, and needs the car\'s network ADB.
Check for updates in the background
Once a day, DiPlay checks GitHub for a new version and shows it on the home screen. It never downloads without your tap.

Stops DiPlay from requesting media audio focus while CarPlay music is active. Enable this if your head unit routes its physical volume buttons to DiPlay and they no longer adjust volume. Steering-wheel play, pause and track controls may stop working on head units that require focus. Applies at the next CarPlay connection.
Use the cover’s color or nearby available car colors. Grey, black or missing covers use all 31 colors; mostly white covers can use white or cold white.
Shows vehicle speed through authorized ADB. Hidden when a reading is unavailable or stale. Changes apply immediately.
Let CarPlay occupy the OEM side-panel area on supported Harman head units. Applies when the CarPlay window next opens; other firmware may display incorrectly.

Names with Chinese or other non-English characters can leave CarPlay on “Getting CarPlay ready…”: some head units broadcast them in a form the iPhone doesn’t find. If that happens, rename the car hotspot with English letters and digits.

Over USB the iPhone can send navigation prompts and Siri’s spoken replies as 8 kHz phone-quality audio. This stops offering 8 and 16 kHz for that audio so the iPhone picks a higher rate. If prompts go silent, turn it off. Reconnects CarPlay.

Shows CarPlay arrows and the next-turn distance in the instrument cluster’s navigation view on FCE head units, by writing to the head unit’s vehicle service. Tested on one car only; turn it off if the cluster behaves unexpectedly.

Show a square album cover over the cluster map. Choose temporary (8 seconds) or permanent artwork; the title and artist always appear over the cover for 8 seconds when the song changes. Position and size apply immediately. Requires cluster projection and iPhone metadata.
Get the report on a phone
Scan the code with the phone camera to open this page in its browser, then choose Download report. Keep this screen open until the download has finished.
Choose USB/CH341 only while a CH341 authentication adapter is connected to the head unit. Without one, choose Local offline. Applies at the next connection.

For an Android phone or tablet used as the head unit: plays CarPlay calls on its loudspeaker instead of the earpiece and uses its hands-free microphone. Leave off on a car head unit. Applies from the next call.
Reduce CarPlay navigation guidance without changing music or call volume. Applies immediately; your head unit’s navigation volume still works.

Turns on the saved car hotspot when DiPlay opens and before a wireless connection. DiPlay needs Android\'s “Modify system settings” access; ADB is not required. To have the hotspot after a full restart, also turn on opening DiPlay after the car starts. The hotspot is not turned off automatically.
“Modify system settings” access is not allowed yet. Allow it so DiPlay can turn on the hotspot.
Pause the car\'s Wi-Fi search during CarPlay · needs ADB

Over Wi-Fi Direct the car searches for Wi-Fi networks every few seconds, and each search makes music and video stutter. With this on, DiPlay pauses the search while CarPlay runs. The car then also does not join a known network, such as your phone\'s hotspot, by itself until CarPlay ends; you can still join one in the car\'s Wi-Fi settings. Turn it off to let the car join automatically. Applies at the next connection.

Shows the DiPlay icon as a bubble over the head unit\'s home screen: tap it to come back to CarPlay and drag it anywhere. It hides as soon as a DiPlay screen is open and comes back when you leave. Hold it to lock its place, hold it again to unlock. Needs \"display over other apps\".

Only for head units that run their hotspot on a network interface Android does not report as a Wi-Fi hotspot, for example eth0.3 on some Geely, Lynk & Co and other Qualcomm units. Leave empty to find it automatically.

BYD head units running Android 10 or later only. Requires approved local ADB. Hides the native call popup while connected CarPlay is in the foreground; restores it in the background. Does not change Bluetooth audio or hide the full phone app.
